title: Just-in-time provisioning trusts an identity-provider claim, and MFA is enforced at enrolment rather than at provisioning
index_line: T-0035 · AUTH_DECISION · any valid assertion from the IdP self-provisions a privileged user; MFA is self-enrolled after · java/c#/python/node · corroborated
invariant_violated: Single sign-on is assumed to make authentication someone else's problem: a valid assertion means a known, vetted user. But auto-provisioning turns *any* assertion into a new account, and the privilege comes from a group claim the attacker's own IdP can carry. Multi-factor is enforced when a user enrols a factor — not when one is provisioned, so the first login of a brand-new account is the one login nobody has to satisfy MFA for.

mechanism.does: the target accepts OIDC logins, with at least one group mapped to a privileged role and group-authenticated logins enabled
an unauthenticated attacker presents an assertion from an identity provider they control, or one whose claims they can shape
the server validates the assertion's signature and issuer but treats the *group/role claim* as authoritative without checking that it should apply here
the login matches the group rule, and the just-in-time provisioning path creates a brand-new account in the privileged group
first login is also the moment the account has no second factor, so the MFA policy is satisfied by enrolling one after the fact
the resulting principal can remote into managed endpoints and run scripts — full control of the fleet the tool was bought to manage

source.http.request.value: the federated login callback: the assertion/token, its claims, and the group rule that maps them to a role

guard.signature.value: the assertion's signature/issuer validation — usually correct, and irrelevant here: the flaw is which claims are trusted and what provisioning does with them

token.claims.value: the group/role claim that decides the provisioned privilege

header.forwarding.value: the redirection/state handling of the OIDC flow — where an attacker-supplied configuration or callback lands

sink.auth.jwt-verify.value: the federated assertion verify/decode call site (OIDC assertion, SAML response, JWT) — the signature check here can be correct while the claims it returns are trusted without a per-provider policy

preconditions.expr: OIDC is enabled and at least one group is mapped to a privileged role with group-authenticated logins allowed
the login path auto-provisions accounts on first sight of an unknown subject
MFA can be enrolled by the user after first login (so a fresh account is un-MFA'd by construction)

check.spec: create a test account through the federated path and check whether the account is usable before any second factor is registered

success: a brand-new privileged account appears in the admin listing with an unfamiliar name/email and no MFA registered
the account is usable immediately after provisioning, before any second-factor enrolment
the login is attributable to a group claim, not to a pre-existing user record
failure_like: provisioning is restricted to a known domain/tenant allow-list, or lands accounts in a non-privileged group
MFA is a precondition of the session rather than an enrolment step
false_positive: a legitimate new joiner created by an administrator — check the IdP's own log for the subject, not just the app's user list
an existing technician whose MFA was reset; the tell for this bug is a *new* account created via the federated path

hazards: the assertion validation can be flawless and the system still be open — triage the *provisioning* decision, not the signature check
group-claim mapping is where multi-tenant SaaS breaks: the claim is true for the attacker's IdP and means nothing for yours
the verify call site is usually fine — the bug is one layer up, in which claims are allowed to map to which role, so 'the signature validates' is not the answer
non_transfers: deployments with no OIDC provider configured, or where group-authenticated login is off
provisioning restricted to an explicit tenant/domain allow-list with role assignment by an administrator
systems that refuse a session until a second factor is enrolled

evidence.target: SimpleHelp <= 5.5.15 and 6.0 pre-release, OIDC login flow (CVE-2026-48558)

provenance.author: Horizon3.ai attack research (CVE-2026-48558 finder)
provenance.corroborates: the three preconditions (OIDC configured, a TechnicianGroup bound to the provider, group-authenticated logins allowed), technician self-provisioning, and the MFA bypass by first-login enrolment
